In one sentence: a role that judges whether agricultural products and agricultural operations comply, using a regulatory basis and reviewable evidence; conclusions must be reviewable, traceable and strictly within the scope of authorisation.

The tasks may involve on-site inspection and recording, product grading and sampling, and reporting and explaining results. The list below is an editorial organisation of sampling-related processes; the U.S. O*NET also lists inspection testing, regulatory enforcement and, for some positions, emergency response and standards work, and actual Chinese inspection is carried out under the law and the assigned duties, so it must not be limited to drafting only.

O*NET 45-2011.00 agricultural inspectors: inspect agricultural products, processing equipment and facilities, and fishing and logging operations to ensure compliance with health, quality and safety laws and regulations. Core tasks include inspecting agricultural products and related operations, interpreting and enforcing government acts and regulations and explaining standards to agricultural workers, checking premises cleanliness and operating practice, verifying that transport and handling procedures meet requirements, and writing inspection-result and remediation-recommendation reports and advising on the corrective measures needed. This profile is a U.S. single-occupation basis, and its inspection authority and procedural framework are not the same as those in mainland China.

entries: Inspection preparation｜Basis and checklist｜First confirm the applicable regulations and standards, turn the requirements into an inspection checklist, and define the inspection object, method and decision basis.

On-site inspection｜Observation and verification｜Check premises cleanliness and operating practice, the condition of processing equipment and facilities, and transport and handling procedures, recording verifiable observations and documents.
Sampling and evidence｜Representative sampling｜Design the sampling frame by batch and risk, avoid taking only the sample that is easiest to obtain, and record the sampling method and location.

Sample chain｜Sealing and handover｜Give each sample a unique number and seal it, and record temperature control, handover signatures and laboratory receipt so the chain of custody can be reconstructed.

Conclusion and remediation｜Non-compliance and deadlines｜Determine the non-compliance items, set out the clause relied on, the remediation recommendation and the deadline, and explain the review and appeal route.
Communication and records｜Explanation and filing｜Explain the standards and requirements to the operator, write and file the inspection report, and keep fact distinct from inference.

Law of the People's Republic of China on the Quality and Safety of Agricultural Products (adopted on 2022, month 9 (September) day 2, in force from 2023, month 1 (January) day 1): producers and operators of agricultural products are responsible for the quality and safety of the products they produce and operate; the agriculture and rural affairs department of the State Council and the market regulation department supervise and administer the quality and safety of agricultural products within the duties assigned by this Law and by regulation; the State establishes a risk monitoring system for the quality and safety of agricultural products and applies source control, risk management and whole-process control. Specific inspection authority, evidence-taking procedure and penalty decisions are carried out under the regulations in force and the competent authority's rules.

First confirm the version of the applicable regulations and standards, the inspection object and the scope of authorisation, and state clearly which evidence-taking methods are permitted and what is prohibited.
Limit the tool to permitted steps, such as form validation, record organisation or first-pass image screening, and do not let it produce a compliance conclusion or penalty recommendation directly.

Paper only throughout. Fictional batch QH-01 has 24 boxes: zone A boxes 1—8, zone B 9—16 and zone C 17—24. The teaching sampling list fixes one box each at 3, 11 and 19, numbered S1, S2 and S3 respectively; it only checks whether the given list covers the three zones, and the list is not called real random sampling or proof of safety representativeness.

Fictional rules Q1: each zone must be covered by one box and the numbers must agree with the sampling form and the receipt log. Q2: the seal must be intact and both parties' handover records complete. Q3: the receipt temperature must be 2—6°C (boundaries included). If any rule is not met, mark it 'exercise to verify'; even if all are met, only 'task-statement record passes' may be marked, and product safety or real compliance cannot be determined.

All inputs: S1 = box 3 / zone A, seal F01 intact, sampling form and receipt log both S1, handover by A and receipt by B both complete, receipt 6°C; S2 = box 11 / zone B, F02 damaged, both numbers S2, handover by A and receipt by B complete, 3°C; S3 = box 19 / zone C, F03 intact, sampling form S3 but receipt log S8, handover by A recorded but receipt by B missing, 8°C. No test result, photograph or real company material is provided.
Deliverables

List the three inspection rules Q1—Q3 and the corresponding fields; for S1—S3 make an 'observation - task-statement rule - evidence - conclusion' four-column table and calculate the three-zone coverage, the sampled-box ratio and the record pass ratio. For each item awaiting verification, state who it should be checked with; do not add to the original record or forge a signature.

Write a summary of 100—150 characters: distinguish zone coverage, sample record conditions and product safety conclusions; explain that test results and a real sampling procedure are missing. Keep the task-statement version, the original log and the human revision list; handwriting or an ordinary table is fine, and no software, real site or regulatory authorisation is required.
Reference check

Q1: S1 and S2 numbers agree; for S3 the sampling form S3 disagrees with the receipt log S8; zones A, B and C are all covered, coverage 3/3=100%, sampled 3/24=12.5%. Q2: S1 passes; S2 seal damaged, to verify; S3 receipt record missing, to verify. Q3: S1 at 6°C is within the inclusive range, S2 at 3°C passes, S3 at 8°C is out of range.

In V1 only S1 satisfies all three rules, a record pass of 1/3=33.33%; S2 is to verify for Q2 and S3 for Q1/Q2/Q3. Check the seals, numbers and handover with the people responsible for the sampling and receipt records, keeping the original records; with no test data and no real procedure, a batch pass, food safety or a rectification deadline cannot be written.
Practice boundaries

Q1—Q3, the temperature range, the box counts, the people and the records are all editorially fictional teaching conditions, not national standards, legal clauses, laboratory receipt procedures or a real sampling quantity. The exercise record pass ratio cannot be used to infer a batch pass rate; real testing bodies work to the specified method, the decision basis and statutory procedure.

values: Day 1｜Read the task and boundaries

Read the complete QH-V1 task statement and list the 24 boxes, the three zones, the fixed sampling list and Q1—Q3; mark the temperature as a fictional rule, and no institutional document is needed and no real site is entered.
Day 2｜Checklist
Break Q1—Q3 into the zone, number, seal, both parties' records and temperature fields; point each item to the original log and add no regulation or testing conclusion.
Day 3｜Paper four-column record
Using the given S1—S3 logs, make an observation-rule-evidence-conclusion table; list the S3/S8 mismatch, the missing receiver and 8°C separately and do not merge away any omission.
Day 4｜Coverage and ratios
Check the three-zone coverage 3/3=100%, the sampling 3/24=12.5% and the V1 all-rules pass 1/3=33.33%; explain that coverage does not prove real representativeness or batch safety.
Day 5｜Single-condition variant

Create only a fictional V2 branch and change the Q3 upper limit from 6 to 5°C (boundaries included), leaving the original log and the other rules unchanged. S1 at 6°C is newly to verify, S2 remains to verify on the seal and S3 on the number/handover/temperature; the pass is 0/3=0%. Keep both V1 and V2, and do not overwrite the original rules or use a changed threshold to handle real product.
Day 6｜Summary and work

Submit the V1/V2 four-column table, the three ratio workings, the anomaly question list and the one-page summary; explain that no test result was provided and that product safety or real compliance cannot be determined.
Day 7｜Self-debrief

Recheck the differences between the two versions independently and record whether you are willing to look up the original numbers, explain the boundaries and keep the uncertain items; the one-week paper exercise is not equivalent to occupational competence, authorisation or passing recruitment.
